## Why This Is Asked

Evaluates practical multi-tenant security controls, policy-as-code, and operational testing in Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts

- Admission control with Gatekeeper or Kyverno
- Namespace RBAC scoping
- Calico NetworkPolicy isolation
- Auditing and runbooks
- CI validation and drift checks

## Code Example

```javascript
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sNSApproved
metadata:
  name: ns-approved
spec:
  match:
    namespaces: ["approved-*"]
```

```javascript
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-privileges
spec:
  rules:
  - name: disallow-privileged
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "Privileged containers are not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

```javascript

kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Ingress","Egress"]
  ingress: []
  egress: []
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical DevOps security skills by testing your ability to implement automated security gates that prevent secret leakage and ensure deployment consistency, directly connecting code hygiene to CI/CD workflows.

## Key Concepts
- Secret scanning integration in CI pipelines
- Baseline management for handling false positives
- Comprehensive coverage of manifests and Helm values
- Local development vs CI environment verification
- Image tag approval and enforcement workflows
- Automated security gates in pull request processes

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions CI Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Secret Scan & Image Validation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
      - '**/values.yaml'
      - '**/Chart.yaml'

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install detect-secrets
        run: pip install detect-secrets

      - name: Scan for secrets
        run: |
          # Initialize baseline if it doesn't exist
          if [ ! -f .secrets.baseline ]; then
            detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline
          fi
          
          # Run scan and fail if new secrets detected
          detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline --all-files
          
          # Check for any high-entropy results
          if detect-secrets audit --report .secrets.baseline | grep -q "High Entropy"; then
            echo "❌ Secrets detected! Please review and remove before merging."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate image tags
        run: |
          # Define approved tags (in production, store this securely)
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest"
          
          # Extract image tags from manifests
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" | \
            sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://' | \
            sort -u > /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          # Validate each tag
          while IFS= read -r tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag '$tag' is not in approved list: $APPROVED_TAGS"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          echo "✅ All image tags are approved"

      - name: Comment on PR (if failed)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🚨 **Security Scan Failed**\n\nThis PR contains either hardcoded secrets or unapproved image tags. Please review the failed job and fix the issues before merging.'
            })
```

### Example Manifest That Would Fail
```yaml
# deployment-with-secrets.yaml (THIS WOULD FAIL THE SCAN)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        # ❌ Unapproved image tag - will fail validation
        image: myregistry/webapp:v1.3.0-beta
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        # ❌ Hardcoded secret - will fail scanning
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          value: "super-secret-password-12345"
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "AKIA1234567890ABCDEFGHI"
        # ❌ Another high-entropy string
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ"
```

### Configuration Files

#### detect-secrets Configuration
```yaml
# .detect-secrets.yml
version: "0.14"
plugins:
  - name: ArtifactoryDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.artifactory
  - name: AWSKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.aws
  - name: Base64HighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "base64"
      min_entropy: 4.5  # Adjust for false positives
  - name: HexHighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "hex"
      min_entropy: 3.0
  - name: KeywordDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.keyword
    keyword_exclude: "passkey,password"  # Add safe keywords
  - name: PrivateKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.private_key
  - name: SlackTokenDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.slack

filters:
  - detect_secrets.filters.common.is_likely_id_string
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_indented_comment
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_potential_uuid
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_sequential_string

# Paths to exclude from scanning
exclude_files:
  - "tests/.*\.mock\.yaml$"
  - "docs/.*\.md$"
```

#### Pre-commit Hook Configuration
```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-secrets
        args: ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline']
  
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-image-tags
        name: Validate image tags
        entry: bash -c '
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest" &&
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" |
          sed "s/.*:\s*//" | sed "s/\"//g" | sed "s/.*://" |
          sort -u | while read tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag \"$tag\" is not approved"
              exit 1
            fi
          done'
        language: system
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

## Local Verification Steps

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
# Install detect-secrets
pip install detect-secrets

# Install pre-commit hooks
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

### 2. Initial Setup
```bash
# Create initial baseline
find . -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | xargs detect-secrets scan > .secrets.baseline

# Review and audit the baseline
detect-secrets audit .secrets.baseline
```

### 3. Test the Workflow
```bash
# Test with a problematic file (should fail)
cat > test-bad.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  password: c3VwZXItc2VjcmV0LXBhc3N3b3JkLTEyMzQ1  # base64 encoded secret
EOF

# Run the scan (should fail)
detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline test-bad.yaml

# Clean up
rm test-bad.yaml
```

### 4. Test Image Tag Validation
```bash
# Create deployment with unapproved tag
cat > test-deployment.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2.0.0  # Not in approved list
EOF

# This should fail the image tag validation
grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" | sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://'

rm test-deployment.yaml
```

## How to Verify in CI

1. **Push a test PR** with problematic files to your fork
2. **Check GitHub Actions** tab to see the security scan job
3. **Verify the job fails** when secrets or unapproved tags are detected
4. **Fix the issues** and push again to confirm the job passes
5. **Review PR comments** for automated notifications when scans fail

## Best Practices

- Store approved image tags in a config file or secret management system
- Use semantic versioning for image tags
- Implement secret management (Kubernetes Secrets, Vault, etc.)
- Regularly update the baseline after auditing
- Enable dependency scanning for container images
- Use image signing and verification for production deployments

Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design comprehensive CI/CD guardrails that ensure security, compliance, and data governance in a complex real-time analytics ecosystem. It tests cross-domain knowledge spanning container security, event streaming architecture, and policy-as-code implementation.

Key Concepts

- Container image security via cosign signing and registry allowlisting
- Data lineage tracking through Kafka topic metadata annotations
- Centralized policy enforcement using OPA/rego policies and Kyverno admission controllers
- Manifest-based validation with clear pass/fail criteria
- CI pipeline integration for automated policy verification

Code Example

```rego
# OPA policy example for Flink job validation
package flink.policy

deny[msg] {
    input.kind == "FlinkDeployment"
    not cosign_signed(input.spec.image)
    msg := "Flink job image must be cosign signed"
}

deny[msg] {
    input.kind == "KafkaTopic"
    not has_lineage_metadata(input.spec.config)
    msg := "Kafka topic must include lineage metadata"
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests end-to-end security design for multi-cloud Kubernetes workloads, focusing on identity, secret management, and policy enforcement with real-world tools.

## Key Concepts
- Zero-trust workload identity (SPIRE)
- Ephemeral credentials (Vault)
- Service mesh security (Istio, mTLS, AuthorizationPolicies)
- Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego)
- Egress controls to data lake and namespace isolation

## Sample Solution

### 1. SPIRE Workload Identity
```yaml
# spire-workload.yaml
apiVersion: spire.spiffe.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterSPIFFEID
metadata:
  name: data-platform-workload
spec:
  names:
    - data-service
    - analytics-service
    - etl-service
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels:
      environment: production
```

### 2. Vault Integration for Secrets
```yaml
# vault-secret-store.yaml
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultSecret
metadata:
  name: data-lake-credentials
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  vaultAddress: https://vault.data-platform.svc.cluster.local:8200
  path: secret/data-lake
  provider: hcp
  refreshInterval: 1h
```

### 3. Istio AuthorizationPolicy
```yaml
# istio-authz.yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: data-lake-access
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: data-lake-gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://data-platform/data-service"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET", "POST"]
        paths: ["/v1/tables/*"]
```

### 4. OPA Policy Example
```rego
#.rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.namespace == "restricted"
  not input.request.object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  msg = "Pods must run as non-root"
}

allow[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  input.request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.privileged
  msg = "Privileged containers not allowed"
}
```

### 5. CI Enforcement Check
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Security Scan
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  opa-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run OPA policy check
        run: |
          opa eval --fail-defined-deny \
            --data policy.rego \
            --input manifests/
```

## Key Takeaways
- SPIRE provides cryptographically secure workload identity
- Vault enables dynamic secret rotation without application changes
- Istio mTLS ensures service-to-service encryption
- OPA/Rego enforces admission control and runtime policies

## Why This Is Asked
Examines ability to design practical, team-wide guardrails at Namespace and Pod levels using policy engines in a real CI flow. Tests understanding of Kubernetes primitives (ResourceQuota, LimitRange, resources, securityContext) and how to surface failures early.

## Key Concepts
- ResourceQuota

```python
# detector.py
import sys, yaml
def has_hostpath(path):
  data = yaml.safe_load(open(path))
  vols = data.get('spec', {}).get('volumes', []) or []
  for v in vols:
    if 'hostPath' in v:
      return True
  return False
if __name__ == '__main__':
  ok = True
  for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    if has_hostpath(f):
      ok = False
      print('HOSTPATH found in', f)
  sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates hands-on policy-as-code skills using Gatekeeper/OPA, Kubernetes security contexts, and CI validation in realistic multi-tenant sandbox environments. It assesses understanding of admission control, namespace isolation, and resource governance.

## Key Concepts

- **ConstraintTemplate vs. Constraint**: A ConstraintTemplate defines the Rego policy logic and CRD schema; a Constraint is a specific instance that applies the policy to matching resources.
- **Kubernetes resource requests/limits**: Requests define minimum guaranteed resources; limits define the maximum resources a container can consume.
- **Security contexts**: These define pod-level and container-level security settings, including running as non-root and read-only filesystems.
- **Namespace isolation**: Gatekeeper policies can target specific namespaces using the `startswith` function to match patterns like `sandbox-*`.
- **Comprehensive validation**: The policy must validate ALL containers in a Deployment, not just check if ANY container meets requirements.

## Evaluation Criteria

A strong answer demonstrates:
1. Correct Rego logic that validates every container (not just the first match)
2. Proper separation between ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
3. Working test cases that actually exercise each validation rule
4. Understanding of the baseline resource concept (50-200% range)
5. CI/CD integration steps for automated validation

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Immutability of container images is a core security practice. This checks a tangible gating mechanism candidates can implement in a simple CI step.

## Key Concepts

- YAML manifest parsing
- Image digest pinning (immutable refs)
- Lightweight CI scripts in GitHub Actions
- Local verification parity with CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (tag-based)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myreg/app:1.2.3
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (digest-based)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myreg/app@sha256:deadbeef...
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this gate to support multi-tenant repos with namespace-scoped images?
- What edge cases or false positives might you address (e.g., external images) and how would you test them?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical gate design for multi-tenant environments with real tooling and secrets handling.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign signature verification against a repository public key
- Digest pinning and non-latest image references in manifests/Helm
- External secrets management (Vault, CSI or AppRole) with projected secrets
- RBAC + admission controls to prevent plaintext secrets
- Local and CI validation workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
name: gate-ci
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup cosign
        run: |
          cosign version
          cosign verify -key cosign.pub registry.example.com/namespace/service@digest
      - name: Lint manifests & charts
        run: |
          helm lint charts/
          yq eval '(.spec.template.spec.containers[].image) != ""' manifests/**/*.yaml
      - name: Validate Vault refs
        run: |
          echo "Vault refs resolved and projected secrets configured" 
```

- How would you rotate the cosign key and propagate it to pipelines?
- How would you detect drift between SBOMs and deployed images at runtime?
